title: Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month FTC - Hull
description:
Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month Fixed-Term Contract Location: Hull, East Yorkshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Full Time 12 Month FTC
Hours: 35 hours per week
Working Pattern: Hybrid / Agile Working
Travel: Regular travel to UK offices, with occasional overnight stays

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a proactive and organised Facilities Coordinator to join the Facilities team of a well-established and forward-thinking legal services organisation based in Hull.

This is a varied and hands-on position, supporting the day-to-day management, maintenance and smooth running of multiple office locations across the UK.

Working closely with colleagues, landlords, contractors and external suppliers, you will help ensure that offices remain safe, compliant, well-maintained and efficient, while supporting facilities projects, office moves and workplace improvements.

Offering hybrid working, an excellent benefits package and exposure to multi-site facilities management, this opportunity would suit someone who enjoys a varied role combining practical problem-solving, facilities administration and health and safety responsibilities.

The Role As Facilities Coordinator, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating day-to-day facilities operations, building maintenance and repairs across multiple UK offices.
- Liaising with landlords, maintenance contractors, suppliers and third-party service providers.
- Supporting workplace health and safety compliance, including risk assessments and workstation assessments.
- Monitoring outstanding actions and ensuring facilities and safety issues are addressed promptly.
- Assisting with office moves, refurbishments, minor maintenance works and facilities improvement projects.
- Maintaining accurate facilities records, compliance documentation and building safety information.
- Supporting the review and development of facilities policies, procedures and processes.
- Managing facilities-related requests and tickets through Salesforce.
- Coordinating and booking complex business travel arrangements.
- Supporting internal and external events and ensuring offices operate effectively.

About You We are looking for a practical, organised and approachable individual who enjoys taking ownership of tasks and ensuring things run smoothly.

Essential requirements:
- Previous experience or a good working knowledge of office health and safety procedures.
- IOSH qualification or currently working towards one.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Confident communication skills and the ability to build relationships with colleagues, contractors and suppliers.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
- A proactive, flexible and hands-on approach to problem-solving.
- Ability to work independently and make sound decisions.
- Full UK driving licence and access to a car.
- Willingness to travel regularly between UK offices, including occasional overnight stays.

Desirable experience:
- Previous experience in Facilities Coordination, Facilities Management or Office Management.
- Knowledge of Health and Safety Executive (HSE) guidance.
- First Aid at Work qualification.
- Fire Marshal training or certification.
- Experience supporting multi-site office operations.

Previous experience within a law firm or legal services organisation is not essential.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- 12-month fixed-term contract.
- Hybrid and agile working arrangements.
- 35-hour working week.
- Private pension.
- Medical insurance.
- Generous annual leave allowance.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunity to gain experience supporting facilities operations across multiple UK locations.

Interested? If you're an experienced Facilities Coordinator, Facilities Assistant, Office Coordinator or Office Manager with a strong understanding of workplace health and safety, I'd be keen to hear from you.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a progressive organisation offering flexibility, variety and a supportive working environment.

title: Senior Administrator
company: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
advertiser_name: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
description: Band 3 Senior Administrator Womens and Childrens Hospital Full Time position Monday to Friday - 8.30 am to 5.00 pm (1 hour lunch break) Are you ready to take the next step in your administrative career and play a vital role in patient care? Our Senior Administrators are the backbone of our services. They support teams, coordinate complex workloads, and ensure clinics and departments run safely and efficiently. They are trusted, reliable and central to the smooth delivery of care. Working within fast-paced and supportive teams, you will take on additional responsibility, helping to oversee processes, support colleagues and ensure patients receive the best possible experience. What we're looking for: Previous administrative experience (NHS experience is welcome but not essential) Strong organisational and prioritisation skills Confidence using IT systems and managing data accurately Excellent communication skills A proactive, solution-focused approach A commitment to teamwork and high standards of service Most importantly, you will understand that behind every task is a patient waiting, and that your role makes a difference. Why join us? Exceptional NHS pension scheme Generous annual leave entitlement Supportive, close-knit teams Ongoing development and progression opportunities A career with purpose Many of our senior managers began their NHS journey in roles just like this. If you are organised, motivated and ready to grow within a service that truly changes lives, this could be your opportunity. For further details with regard to this vacancy opportunity, please see the attached Job Description and Person Specification. We reserve the right to close the advert early in the event of high levels of interest. Therefore, early applications are encouraged. Please note that, in line with UKVI regulations, this vacancy does not meet the eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker Visa route. As a result, we are unable to issue a Certificate of Sponsorship for this position. We remain committed to fair and equal recruitment practices and encourage applications from all suitably qualified candidates who have the right to work in the UK.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are seeking a dedicated and professional Part-Time Medical Receptionist to join our healthcare team here at The Avenues Medical Centre. The ideal candidate will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors, providing exceptional customer service while managing administrative tasks efficiently. This role is crucial in ensuring smooth operations within the GP Practice and enhancing the patients experience. Greet patients and visitors warmly, professionally and friendly ensuring a welcoming environment Manage patient check-in and check-out processes, including verifying personal information and contact details. Assisting patients using the self check-in machine in the waiting room Schedule appointments, confirm bookings, and handle cancellations or rescheduling requests Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality in accordance with the data protection regulations Answer phone calls promptly, addressing inquiries or directing calls to appropriate staff members. Including patient call backs Process incoming mail and manage correspondence effectively Process medication requests from patients Maintain an organised reception area, ensuring it is tidy and well-stocked adhering to the surgeries Clear Desk Policy Collaborate with healthcare professionals to facilitate efficient patient flow within the practice Utilise the use of our Extended Access Appointments & CDC Centre Follow and adhere to all Practice Processes, Protocols, SOPs & Practice Policies. You will also be required to keep up to date with any changes Manage the Reception Teams generic email account, action all emails accordingly and in a timely manner. Signpost and Care Navigate patients to the most appropriate care/service. This may include a Pharmacy First Referral etc Responsibilities: Manage patient check-in and check-out processes, including verifying personal information and contact details. This would also include updating the patients records where needed. Assisting patients using the self check-in machine in the waiting room Arrange/book interpreters where needed for patients using AA Global either booking via their online portal or over the telephone Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality in accordance with the data protection regulations/GDPR. Document clearly & accurately Checking on the patients record if Third Party Consent has been granted if you are not speaking to the patient directly. Should no consent be documented on the record follow the practice policy and adhere to Data Protection, GDPR and Patient Confidentiality Process incoming mail either by internal post or external post and manage correspondence effectively. Opening, date stamping, initialing and passing all documents onto the correct team Process medication requests from patients face to face at the front reception desk, online requests via System Online or the NHS App, email, telephone (certain cohorts of patients only) or paper requests Maintain an organised reception area, ensuring it is tidy and well-stocked with necessary materials adhering to the surgeries Clear Desk Policy Accepting samples at the front reception desk following the practice process and passing onto the nursing team to action Utilise the use of our Extended Access Appointments on remote booking & CDC Centre Undertake mandatory training either online or face to face when required and keeping up to date with all training. You will also be required to monitor when your training is due for renewal. Attend PTL afternoons Follow and adhere to all Practice Processes, Protocols, SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) and Practice Policies. You will also be required to keep up to date with any changes/updates Process cash payments for Non-NHS Private work from patients which is chargeable following the practice Private Charges list. Being responsible for issuing the patient with a receipt of payment, log/document in the patients record and place all monies in the secure Private Money Box, maintaining the money is kept secure & safe. Support the GP Partners and Nursing Team to chaperone in appointments as needed once you have undertaken the relevant training. Signpost and Care Navigate patients to the most appropriate care/service. This may include a Pharmacy First Referral, signpost to NHS111, Urgent Care etc Action tasks and other duties assigned to your work station that day.
